title: Distributor and Stockist Order-Taking Voice Agent
summary: A voice and WhatsApp agent that takes orders from stockists and chemists by brand and pack, checks stock, schemes and credit, reads the order back and posts it to your ERP or DMS.

seo.title: Stockist Order-Taking Voice Agent for Pharma | VipraTech
seo.description: Voice agent that takes stockist and chemist orders in Hindi and regional languages, checks stock, schemes and credit, and posts orders to your ERP.

problem.intro: Pharma companies in India sell through carrying and forwarding agents, stockists and retail chemists. Stockist orders still arrive as calls to the depot, handwritten slips carried by MRs, or WhatsApp photos of order books, and depot staff key them into the ERP or distributor management system.

pain_points.title: Orders by phone and photo
pain_points.detail: Order lines arrive as brand nicknames and pack sizes, spoken quickly or written by hand, and get keyed with errors.

pain_points.title: Scheme confusion
pain_points.detail: Stockists ask about running schemes and free-goods offers, and the answer depends on who picks up the phone.

pain_points.title: Stock and credit surprises
pain_points.detail: Orders are accepted for products out of stock at the depot or for stockists over their credit limit, and get cut later.

pain_points.title: MRs carrying orders
pain_points.detail: Field reps spend time relaying orders between chemists and stockists instead of focusing on doctor calls.

solution.overview: We build an ordering agent that stockists and chemists can call, or message on WhatsApp, in Hindi, English or a regional language. It recognises the customer from the registered number, understands brand names, strengths and pack sizes including common shorthand, and reads back each line. Before confirming, it checks depot stock, current schemes and the stockist's credit status in your ERP, and offers substitutes only from your approved list. Confirmed orders are posted to the ERP or DMS with a WhatsApp acknowledgement. Unclear lines, credit holds and requests outside policy go to depot staff.
capabilities: Takes orders by inbound call, scheduled outbound call or WhatsApp voice and text
Understands brand, strength and pack names, including common shorthand and Hinglish
Reads back each order line, free goods and expected value before confirmation
Checks depot stock, running schemes and credit status in your ERP
Posts confirmed orders to the ERP or distributor management system
Hands credit holds, disputes and unclear lines to depot staff with a call summary

workflow.title: Stockist calls or messages
workflow.detail: The agent identifies the stockist from the registered number and loads their account context.

workflow.title: Capture order lines
workflow.detail: The stockist speaks or types order lines, and the agent matches each to a SKU, asking about any it is unsure of.

workflow.title: Check stock, schemes and credit
workflow.detail: Each line is checked against depot stock, applicable schemes and the stockist's credit status.

workflow.title: Route exceptions
workflow.detail: Credit holds, unmatched products and special requests go to depot staff with the call summary.

workflow.title: Read back and confirm
workflow.detail: The agent reads back lines, free goods and expected value, and the stockist confirms.

workflow.title: Post and acknowledge
workflow.detail: The confirmed order is posted to the ERP, and a WhatsApp acknowledgement with the order number is sent.

inputs: Stockist and chemist master with registered numbers and licence details
Product master with brand, strength, pack and common aliases
Credit limits and outstanding balances from the ERP
outputs: Confirmed orders posted to ERP or DMS
Exception tickets for credit holds and unclear lines
Demand signals for lines that could not be supplied
human_in_the_loop: Depot staff resolve every credit hold, unmatched product and non-standard request before the order is confirmed. Scheme rules and substitute lists are set and approved by the commercial team, not by the agent.
integrations: ERP such as SAP, Tally or a pharma distribution ERP
CRM holding the stockist and chemist master
guardrails: Every order read back and confirmed before posting
Substitutes offered only from an approved list
No discounts or schemes beyond configured rules
No medical or dosing advice; such questions are declined and redirected
Calls recorded with notice and retained per policy
compliance_notes: Designed to accept orders only from stockists and chemists whose drug licence details are on file in your master, with special-category products excluded where your controls require it.
Outbound calls follow TRAI commercial communication rules and customer preferences, and personal data is processed in line with the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: One depot or C&F location and a group of its stockists for one product division, with orders also logged by the usual route for comparison.
deliverables: Product alias dictionary for the pilot division
Working voice and WhatsApp ordering agent
ERP or DMS integration in a test environment

what_we_measure.how: Lines captured by the agent compared with the confirmed order in the ERP after depot review.
Orders needing depot staff intervention, grouped by reason.
Time from call start to confirmed order, from call logs.
Stockists placing repeat orders through the agent during the pilot.

faqs.q: Can it understand brand nicknames and short forms?
faqs.a: Yes. We build an alias dictionary from your past orders and depot staff knowledge. When a name matches more than one SKU, the agent asks a clarifying question.

faqs.q: What about narcotic, psychotropic or other controlled products?
faqs.a: Ordering follows your existing controls. Products that need special handling can be excluded from the agent and routed to depot staff.

faqs.q: Will stockists accept talking to an AI?
faqs.a: The agent tells callers it is automated and offers a human handover at any point. The pilot measures repeat usage so you can judge adoption with real data.
No. It is an ordering front end that posts to your existing ERP or DMS. Pricing, schemes and invoicing stay in those systems.
